title: Learning from a lost support
literal_meaning: A blind person loses the walking stick once.
explanation: Losing something relied upon can make a person more careful afterwards. The saying compresses that lesson into the loss of a walking stick. It is a figurative warning about repeating mistakes, not a factual assertion about blind people or a guarantee that a loss happens only once.
meaning_odia: ଏକଥର କ୍ଷତି ସହିବା ପରେ ସେହି ଭୁଲ ପୁଣି ନ କରିବାକୁ ସତର୍କ ହେବା।
usage_example: After losing an unsigned draft, a writer starts saving a dated copy after each session. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The wording uses blindness and a stick as an image of dependence on a support. Explain the image without reducing blind people to helplessness or using it to mock disability.
